result.answer: Today the demo bed-management system is set to keep only the patient's current location. Under that setting, Shutter closed the case with nothing sent. The WARD-B move (08:20 UTC, 15 Oct 2026) was overtaken by the WARD-C move (08:45 UTC), which was applied. If the system had to keep every movement, the case would have gone to a person instead of closing (W1). That person would cancel the WARD-C transfer, then replay both moves in order. That setting is not in force now. Changing it is a draft for a person to review on the Site profile page. It would affect every overtaken failure on this route. All three members agree on this outcome. They differ on emphasis. Conformance says the message itself was fine and the failure came from the receiver being unavailable. The Encounter review points out that the plan quotes epoch 79 and a freshness time on 25 Oct. The record that was actually read shows epoch 94, current until 03:16:41 UTC on 1 Nov. Impact warns that a cancel and replay could set off extra pharmacy or porter actions for a patient already on WARD-C. That is an inference, and Shutter cannot see those systems. I cannot change the setting or act on the case.

perspectives.view: The message is a valid transfer and the failure was the receiver being unavailable, not the content. Keeping a full history would send the case to a person (W1). Whether the move should be recorded is for the other reviews.

The WARD-B move has been overtaken by the applied WARD-C move. Under a full-history setting it would still matter as a past event and would go to a person (W1). The plan's epoch 79 and 25 Oct freshness do not match the values read (epoch 94, 1 Nov), though the outcome stays the same.

Under W1 the case goes to a person, and that is all Shutter can state. A cancel and replay might, by inference, trigger needless pharmacy redirections and porter tasks. Today, doing nothing leaves the record correct on WARD-C.

setting.why: The receiver's category, current_state (keep only the current location), is why the case closed as superseded.

under_alternative.why: As history_of_record, the case would have gone to a person instead of closing with no write.

suggested_change.why: It matches keeping every movement: change Downstream Out to history_of_record. This is a draft for review on the Site profile page.

response.content: I submitted the board's answer for C-000129: under a full movement history setting (W1), the case would have gone to a person instead of closing, and all three specialists' differing views are kept in it.
